newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo precious metals slip, led by platinum.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo precious metals slip, led by platinum.

text.p: Tokyo precious metals futures, led by falls in platinum futures, ended lower across the board on Thursday pressured by the yen's firmer tone against the dollar and weaker New York prices overnight, traders said.
Gold prices ranged from four to six yen per gram lower. Benchmark August was four yen down at 1,357 yen.
Platinum prices ranged from four to 10 yen per gram weaker. Benchmark August was down eight at 1,369 yen.
"The view that dollar gains have stalled prompted local investors to sell platinum futures. Sentiment in platinum was bearish with little incentive to buy," one trader said.

Some traders said platinum futures prices were likely to be cheaper than gold futures, as large long positions still held by individual investors, especially in the December contract, were weighing on the market.
Talks of steady Russian sales of white group metals, and lacklustre demand also undermined sentiment in platinum.
In the gold futures market, traders noted mixed trade by private investors.
Bullion was quoted slightly weaker at $380.60/90 per ounce at the Tokyo close, against $380.90/381.40 in New York on Wednesday.
One trader said the weaker spot silver price was likely to pressure sentiment in other precious metals.
Silver futures ranged from 0.7 yen to 2.3 yen per 10 grams weaker. Benchmark August was 0.8 yen lower at 182.3 yen.
Palladium futures ranged from one to six yen per gram lower. Benchmark August was one yen lower at 418 yen.
